title: Design layered variables: multi-task evidence graphs over mentions
description: Today an EvidenceGraph binds one Task: every claim, including supporting claims, must match its answer schema, so a derived variable cannot cite intermediate variables with their own schemas. Mention is unimplemented, and mention IDs are not evidence IDs. Inference records only a free-text rationale. Design (contract change in docs/02, no implementation yet): (1) declared variable dependency graph: variables with answer schemas and permitted input variables; (2) multi-task graph context where each claim validates against its own task and inference inputs respect the declared dependencies; (3) the mention layer: Mention model and an explicit policy for how a mention and its attributes become cited Inclusions or mention-level claims; (4) typed derivation provenance (rule or model id, version, inputs), replayable for deterministic rules; (5) unchanged guarantees: acyclicity, case scope, source-backed leaves, outcomes and final-claim IDs per variable; (6) how Example, CaseResult, store tables, and Loupe review represent multi-variable cases. Keep note scope; patient-level aggregation stays deferred but must not be precluded. Timebox: decide the shapes that bpr.2/bpr.3/bpr.4 must not preclude.
acceptance_criteria: Contract amendment in docs/02 (and docs/00 if needed) with rationale and synthetic examples; follow-up implementation issues filed; bpr.2 can proceed without precluding the design.
